title: Stale-While-Revalidate: Savings Grid and Hit-Rate Scenarios (Q2 2026)
summary: Exploratory savings workbook that models the impact of introducing a stale-while-revalidate (SWR) serving policy on top of our prefix/KV cache for read-heavy and bursty workloads. The sheet compares baseline hit-rates (no SWR) to multiple SWR tuning points across customer segments and query types, projecting token-level cost and net savings over a 30-day window.

assumptions: Cost per 1k tokens is set to $0.02 (hosted average); SWR improves observed hit-rates by preventing immediate re-fetches for requests within the stale window; KV retention unchanged but effective hit% increases due to serving stale KV while background refresh happens; request volume held constant (we only model token-level savings, not changes in downstream behavior); no pricing changes or prefetching costs modeled; background revalidations consume the same token costs as a regular request (conservative).
recommended_actions: 1) Pilot SWR with 3 buckets: short (s=10s), medium (s=60s), long (s=180s) across 3 customers representative of Enterprise/search, Mobile-chat, Internal-tools; 2) Instrument exact revalidation token counts (background refresh per key) and add that cost to the next iteration; 3) Implement metric set: per-key revalidate-rate, stale-serving ratio, end-to-end latency P95; 4) Combine SWR with per-segment TTL heuristics (short = low-latency; long = high-cost-savings); 5) Prepare rollback plan: automatic disable if post-SWR error rate increases >0.5% or latency P99 regresses by >100ms.
notes: Preliminary numbers are from sampling logs (Jan–Feb 2026) and conservative SWR multipliers from lab A/B tests. Open questions: how often background refreshes will cause request spikes on model endpoints; interactions with autoscaling (revalidation batches may trigger transient scale-ups); legal/consistency implications for regulated customers (phrase as opt-in); next update should add a column for background revalidation token cost and model fallback penalty.
